title: WPMS/3281/2018 of AJAY JAISWAL Vs RETURNING OFFICER (URBAN LOCAL BODIES)/SUB DIVISIONAL MAGISTRATE SITARGANJ

paras.text:
WPMS No. 3281 of 2018
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Mr. Subhash Upadhayaya, Advocate with Mr.
Rahul Consul, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for the
State/respondent nos.1, 4 and 7.
 Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Advocate for respondent no.2.
 Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the caveator/
private respondent.
 The nomination paper of the petitioner has been
rejected in the ongoing process for local body election
for the post of Chairman, Nagar Panchayat, Shaktigarh.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition
challenging rejection of his nomination paper.
 Rejection of nomination paper of a candidate in
an election may be on totally arbitrariness or even
imaginable ground, and be even mala fide, yet though
it can be a ground in an election petition at an
appropriate stage, but, once the election process is
already on, no interference on the validity of the
rejection of the nomination paper can be undertaken by
any Court including this Court, in view of the seminal
decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election
Commissioner, New Delhi reported in (1978) 1 SCC
405 affirming its earlier decision in the case of N.P.
Ponnuswami v. The Returning Officer, Namakkal
Constituency, Namakkal, Salem Dist. and others
reported in AIR 1952 SC 64, cover the field.
 In view of the above, writ petition is liable to be
dismissed and it is hereby dismissed.
